author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing serves a page below the first as the first page
summary: A request for the owner listing at a page below the first is listed as the first page of matching owners instead of failing to an error page.
acceptance_criteria: given the owner listing asked for at page zero, when the request runs, then the first page of matching owners is listed rather than an error page
given the owner listing asked for at a negative page, when the request runs, then the first page of matching owners is listed rather than an error page
given the owner listing asked for at a page below the first, when the listing is shown, then it presents itself as the first page rather than as the page asked for
given a page below the first, when the search names a last name and when it is empty, then both list the first page
non_goals: behavior for a page above the last page
behavior for a page value that is not a number
notes: Bug fix confirmed by the owner's report; the requirement is new, so no PRD requirement is superseded. Scope is bounded to the quoted request: the owner listing and page values below the first. Three deliberate omissions are recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md rather than absorbed. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice is a defect in one existing seam and needs no new design ground. docs/system-design.md § Contracts already carries OwnerController as the owner listing's server-rendered surface, and architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog (Web controller, in force) already assigns request binding, delegation, and response selection to it. The listing reads its page from a request parameter and converts it to a zero-based Pageable in the controller's own pagination helper; the requested value below the first page is what makes that conversion throw. Normalizing the parameter to the first page before it is used is request binding under that same catalog row, not a new rule: the same method already normalizes the other listing parameter by stripping the last name (OwnerController.java:103). No domain rule, type, package, or dependency moves. Resolution basis is grep plus a full read of OwnerController.java (headless run, no IDE oracle connected) — the weaker basis, so the covering symbol was read rather than recalled. The only docs write is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Contracts row.
integration_points: OwnerController.processFindForm binds the page parameter and is the single point both the query and the view model flow through
OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName converts the page to a zero-based PageRequest — the throw site today
OwnerController.addPaginationModel publishes currentPage, which owners/ownersList.html uses to render the page links and the first/previous controls

patterns.description: Web controller (in force): adapts one HTTP surface — binds the request, delegates, selects the response. Parameter normalization at the boundary belongs here; a business rule does not.
existing request-parameter normalization in the same method (last name stripped before the query) — the precedent the page normalization follows

risks.risk: Normalizing inside the pagination helper alone satisfies the HTTP 200 criteria while leaving the published currentPage at the value asked for, which fails the third acceptance criterion and renders the template's first/previous controls against a page that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once in processFindForm before the value reaches either collaborator, so the query and the view model agree (docs/system-design.md § Contracts: OwnerController owns search with paging; architecture-principles § Design Principles 6, understandable systems).

risks.risk: A reviewer may read the normalization as a business rule added to a controller, which architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog forbids as a fresh violation.
risks.mitigation: Keep it a pure transport-parameter normalization stated at the binding boundary and delegate unchanged; no domain state is branched on, and the Web controller row assigns binding to the controller.

risks.risk: The veterinarian listing converts its page the same way (VetController.java:61) and would throw identically; the slice's non-goals exclude it.
risks.mitigation: Leave VetController untouched and do not extract a shared pagination helper in this slice (prd-entry non-goal: paging of the veterinarian directory).

risks.risk: Until fixed, the thrown conversion reaches the error page, which renders the exception message to the reader.
risks.mitigation: The fix removes an input-reachable path into that page; the error page's own disclosure stays open as recorded (docs/system-design.md § Known Defects, REQ-SYS-002 row; architecture-principles § Design Principles 7, fail secure).

Design write applied: REQ-OWN-005 added to the OwnerController row in docs/system-design.md § Contracts. author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and the reviewer has no network access. The change set touches no build file and adds no dependency, so there is no supply-chain delta for this slice; the standing gap belongs to CI, not to this change.

A page above the last page still yields an empty Page and rejects the search with the notFound message rather than listing the last page, and a non-numeric page still throws into the disclosing error page. Both are pre-existing and both are recorded as PRD open questions; neither is a finding against this diff, but the non-numeric case keeps a request-reachable route into the error page that this slice's rationale otherwise closes.
approved_aspects: Boundary normalization is the correct placement: the request-derived page is clamped once in processFindForm before it reaches either collaborator, so no downstream caller can be handed an unvalidated value (OwnerController.java:109).

Attack surface narrows rather than widens: page=0 and page=-3 previously reached PageRequest.of with a negative index, throwing IllegalArgumentException into the error page, which docs/security-principles.md records as rendering the underlying exception message. The clamp removes that input-reachable disclosure path without touching the recorded baseline defect itself.
No integer-overflow or unbounded-allocation path introduced: Math.max(page, 1) keeps page-1 >= 0, and the page size stays a fixed literal 5, so a caller cannot enlarge the result set.

Data access still runs through the derived repository query findByLastNameStartingWith with a bound Pageable; no query text is concatenated and no request-derived value composes a path or resource name.
No new endpoint, no widened management exposure, no new credential, no logging of request values, no serialization or template-expression evaluation added.

Tests exercise the boundary through the real MVC binding and dispatch via MockMvc and assert the value actually handed to the repository (ArgumentCaptor on Pageable), so the security-relevant claim is verified at the boundary rather than restated.
Documentation changes are prose only, with the two unresolved input cases (page above the last, non-numeric page) recorded as open questions rather than silently implied to be handled.
